draft.title: Exploring space
card: collect light and other radiation from far away. They let scientists study distant stars and galaxies without leaving Earth, or from orbit above the atmosphere.
uncrewed spacecraft sent to planets, moons and other bodies. They carry instruments to measure and photograph what they find, and send the data back to Earth.
carry people into space. Astronauts can run experiments and make decisions on the spot, such as on the International Space Station.
Space research can also lead to everyday technology. Better solar cells are one example, now used in homes on Earth.
draft.remember: Telescopes, probes and crewed missions each study space in their own way, and the research can lead to useful technology on Earth.

a.q: Which tool is an uncrewed spacecraft sent to measure and photograph a planet up close?
a.why: A probe travels to a planet or moon and sends data back to Earth. A telescope collects radiation from far away and does not travel to the body it studies.
a.clue: Think about which tool travels to the planet without people on board.

b.q: A space agency wants to study a distant galaxy over many years, without sending anything to it. Which method fits best, and why?
opts: A telescope, because it collects radiation from far away
A probe, because it can fly to the galaxy and take samples
A crewed mission, because people can fly out to the galaxy
A solar cell, because it records light from the galaxy
b.why: A telescope collects light and other radiation, so it can study a galaxy from far away. A probe is the tempting choice, but it is built to travel to nearby bodies such as planets and moons, not to reach a distant galaxy.
b.clue: Which tool studies things without travelling to them?

b.best: A telescope, because it collects radiation from far away
